chapters.n: Peter, the senior Apostle, writes to believers spread across five Roman provinces in what is now Turkey. He calls them “strangers”—people whose true home is with God.

f.g: Temporary residents, exiles living away from home.

f.w: Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia
f.g: Roman provinces in Asia Minor (modern Turkey).

chapters.n: These Saints were chosen in God’s plan, made holy by the Spirit, and called to obey Christ and be cleansed by His blood. All three members of the Godhead are named.

f.g: Echoes covenant rites where blood was sprinkled on the people.

chapters.n: Peter bursts into praise: in His great mercy God has given us a new birth into a living hope, made possible because Jesus rose from the dead.

f.g: Born again; given new spiritual life.

chapters.n: That hope is an inheritance that can’t decay, be stained, or fade—kept safe in heaven for you.
And you yourselves are guarded by God’s power through your faith until the full salvation is revealed at the end.

f.g: Guarded, as by a military garrison.

chapters.n: This hope brings deep joy, even though for a little while you may be weighed down by many kinds of trials.
Gold is refined by fire, yet gold eventually perishes. Your tested faith is far more precious, and it will bring praise and glory when Jesus Christ appears.
Though you have never seen Jesus, you love Him and believe in Him, and you are filled with a joy too glorious for words.
The result of your faith is the salvation of your souls.

f.g: The goal or outcome of faith.

chapters.n: Ancient prophets searched carefully about this salvation and the grace that would come to you.
The Spirit of Christ in those prophets testified in advance of Christ’s sufferings and the glory afterward. Latter-day Saints see this fulfilled in Book of Mormon prophets too.
The prophets knew they were serving future generations. The same message has now been preached to you by the Holy Ghost—truths even angels long to understand.

f.g: To stoop and peer into, as if leaning to see more clearly.

chapters.n: So get your minds ready for action, stay clear-headed, and set your hope fully on the grace you will receive when Jesus Christ is revealed.

f.w: gird up the loins of your mind
f.g: Tuck up your long robe to move freely—be mentally prepared.

chapters.n: Be like obedient children and don’t shape your lives around the desires you followed before you knew the gospel.
Since the God who called you is holy, become holy in every part of your conduct.
Peter quotes the command God gave Israel: be holy, because I am holy.
If you call on a Father who judges everyone fairly by their deeds, then live your time here on earth with reverence.
You were rescued from the empty lifestyle passed down by your ancestors—not with silver or gold, which wear out.

f.g: Bought back, ransomed, as from slavery.

chapters.n: Instead, you were redeemed by Christ’s precious blood, like a flawless Passover lamb. His sacrifice is the price of our freedom.
Christ was chosen for this mission before the world was created, but He has come in these last times for your sake. Latter-day Saints connect this to the premortal council.

f.w: foreordained before the foundation of the world

chapters.n: Through Christ you believe in the God who raised Him from the dead and glorified Him, so your faith and hope rest in God.

f.w: raised him up from the dead

chapters.n: Having cleansed your souls by obeying the truth, you now have sincere love for fellow believers. So love one another deeply, from a pure heart.

f.g: Intensely, stretched out to the full.

chapters.n: You have been born again from a seed that can’t die—the living and lasting word of God.
Peter quotes Isaiah: people and their glory are like grass and wildflowers that wither and fall.
But the Lord’s word lasts forever—and that enduring word is the very gospel that was preached to you.
So get rid of every kind of ill will, deceit, pretending, jealousy, and gossip—habits that poison a community of believers.
Like newborn babies crave milk, crave the pure nourishment of God’s word so you can grow spiritually.
If you have already tasted how kind the Lord is, you will want more.

f.w: tasted that the Lord is gracious

chapters.n: Come to Christ, the living stone—rejected by people but chosen and treasured by God.
You also are living stones being built into a spiritual temple and a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices God accepts through Jesus Christ.
Scripture says God would lay a precious cornerstone in Zion; whoever trusts in Him will never be put to shame.
To believers, Christ is precious. To those who reject Him, He is still the stone the builders threw out that became the most important stone of all.
For the disobedient, Christ becomes a stone they trip over. Rejecting His word leads to a fall—the natural result of disobedience.
Peter gives believers Israel’s titles: chosen, royal priests, a holy nation, God’s own special people—called to proclaim Him who brought them from darkness into light.

f.g: Not ‘odd’ but ‘God’s own possession,’ a treasured people.

chapters.n: Once you were not a people; now you are God’s people. Once you had not received mercy; now you have.
As temporary residents on earth, keep away from bodily cravings that wage war against your soul.
Live honorably among unbelievers. Even if they slander you now, your good deeds may lead them to glorify God when He visits.
For the Lord’s sake, respect human government, beginning with the emperor.
Respect governors, too, who are sent to punish wrongdoers and praise those who do right.
God wants your good conduct to silence the ignorant accusations of foolish people.
You are free, but don’t use freedom as a cover for doing wrong. Live as God’s servants.

f.g: A disguise or excuse for evil.

chapters.n: Four short commands: respect everyone, love fellow believers, reverence God, and honor the emperor.
Household servants—many were slaves in the Roman world—should respect their masters, even harsh ones. Peter addresses life as it was, not endorsing slavery.
God approves when someone, mindful of Him, bears unjust suffering patiently.
There is no credit in enduring a beating you deserved. But patiently suffering for doing good pleases God.
This is what you were called to, because Christ suffered for you and left an example so you could follow in His footsteps.
Jesus never sinned and never spoke a deceitful word.

f.w: neither was guile found in his mouth

chapters.n: When insulted, He didn’t insult back. When He suffered, He made no threats but trusted Himself to God, the righteous Judge.
Christ personally carried our sins in His body on the cross, so that we could die to sin and live for righteousness. By His wounds we are healed.

f.w: by whose stripes ye were healed

chapters.n: You were like wandering sheep, but now you have returned to Christ, the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
Peter addresses wives, especially those married to husbands who weren’t believers. In that culture, a wife’s respectful, Christlike conduct might win her husband to the gospel without preaching.

f.g: Respectful order within the household, as understood in that culture.

chapters.n: Husbands would notice their wives’ pure and reverent way of living.
True beauty shouldn’t depend on elaborate hairstyles, gold jewelry, or expensive clothes—the status symbols of the Roman world.

f.g: Braiding hair into elaborate styles, often woven with gold or pearls.

chapters.n: Instead, let your beauty be the inner person—a gentle and peaceful spirit that never fades and that God treasures.
Holy women of ancient times, who trusted God, showed this same inner beauty in their marriages.
Sarah honored Abraham, and believing women become her spiritual daughters as they do good and refuse to be ruled by fear.
Husbands must live with their wives with understanding and honor, treating them as equal heirs of eternal life. Mistreating a wife damages a man’s prayers.

f.g: Likely refers to physical strength and social vulnerability, not worth.

chapters.n: To everyone: be united, sympathetic, loving like family, tenderhearted, and humble.
Don’t pay back evil with evil or insult with insult. Instead, bless—because you were called to inherit a blessing.
Peter quotes Psalm 34: whoever wants a good life must keep their tongue from evil and their lips from lies.

f.w: love life, and see good days

chapters.n: Turn away from evil, do good, and actively pursue peace.
The Lord watches over the righteous and hears their prayers, but He sets His face against evildoers.
Generally, who will hurt you if you are eager to do good?
Even if you do suffer for doing right, you are blessed. Don’t fear what your opponents fear or be shaken.

f.w: be not afraid of their terror

chapters.n: Honor Christ as Lord in your hearts, and always be ready to explain the hope you have—gently and respectfully. This is a favorite verse for missionaries and members alike.
Keep a clear conscience so that people who slander you will be ashamed when they see your good Christian conduct.
If you must suffer, it’s better to suffer for doing good than for doing wrong.
Christ suffered once for sins—the Righteous One for the unrighteous—to bring us to God. His body died, but He was made alive by the Spirit.
In the spirit, Christ went and preached to spirits in prison. Latter-day Saints see this as His visit to the spirit world between His death and Resurrection.
These spirits had disobeyed in Noah’s day, when God patiently waited while the ark was built. Only eight people were saved through the water.
The Flood is a type of baptism. Baptism saves not by washing dirt from the body, but as a pledge of a clean conscience to God, made effective by Christ’s Resurrection.

f.g: Greek antitypos — a corresponding pattern or symbol.

f.w: baptism doth also now save us

chapters.n: Jesus has ascended to heaven and sits at God’s right hand, with angels and every power subject to Him.
Since Christ suffered in His body, arm yourselves with the same attitude. Someone willing to suffer rather than sin has broken sin’s hold.
So spend the rest of your earthly life doing God’s will instead of chasing human cravings.
You have spent enough of your past living like pagans—in sensuality, drunkenness, wild parties, and idol worship.
Your old friends are surprised you no longer join their reckless living, and they speak badly of you for it.
But they will answer to Christ, who is ready to judge the living and the dead.

f.w: judge the quick and the dead

chapters.n: This is why the gospel was preached even to the dead—so they could be judged fairly like the living and live spiritually with God. This verse underlies the Latter-day Saint practice of work for the dead.

f.w: preached also to them that are dead

chapters.n: The end of all things is near, so stay clear-minded and watchful in prayer.
Above all, keep loving each other deeply, because love covers over many sins.

f.w: charity shall cover the multitude of sins

chapters.n: Open your homes to one another without complaining.

f.g: Literally ‘love of strangers’; vital for traveling missionaries and house churches.

chapters.n: Each person has received a gift from God. Use it to serve others as faithful managers of God’s many-sided grace.
Whoever speaks should speak as one delivering God’s words; whoever serves should rely on God’s strength. Then God gets the glory through Jesus Christ.
Don’t be shocked by the fiery ordeal testing you, as if something unusual were happening.
Instead, rejoice to share in Christ’s sufferings, so that you will be overjoyed when His glory is revealed.
If you are insulted for Christ’s name, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.
Make sure you never suffer for being a murderer, thief, criminal, or meddler in other people’s business.
But if you suffer for being a Christian, don’t be ashamed. Praise God that you carry that name. This is one of only three New Testament uses of the word “Christian.”
Judgment begins with God’s own household. If believers are refined first, what will happen to those who reject the gospel?
Quoting Proverbs, Peter notes that if the righteous are saved only with difficulty, the ungodly face far worse.
So those suffering according to God’s will should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and keep doing good.
Peter humbly speaks as a fellow elder to the Church’s leaders. He saw Christ’s sufferings firsthand and will share in His coming glory.

f.w: witness of the sufferings of Christ

chapters.n: Shepherd God’s flock willingly—not because you must, not for money, but eagerly. Peter echoes Jesus’s charge to him to “feed my sheep.”
Don’t boss people around; lead by being an example to the flock.
When Christ, the Chief Shepherd, appears, faithful leaders will receive a crown of glory that never fades.
Younger members should respect the older leaders. Everyone should wear humility like clothing, because God opposes the proud but helps the humble.

f.g: Tie it on like a servant’s apron.

chapters.n: Humble yourselves under God’s powerful hand, and He will lift you up at the right time.
Throw all your worries onto God, because He genuinely cares about you.

f.w: Casting all your care upon him

chapters.n: Stay clear-headed and alert. The devil, your enemy, prowls like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour.

f.g: Opponent in a lawsuit; an accuser.

chapters.n: Resist him with firm faith, remembering that believers everywhere are going through the same kinds of suffering.
After you have suffered a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to His eternal glory in Christ, will Himself restore, strengthen, and settle you firmly.

f.g: Set you on a firm foundation.

chapters.n: Peter closes with praise: to God belongs glory and power forever.
Peter wrote this short letter with the help of Silvanus (Silas), a trusted companion, to encourage them and testify that this is God’s true grace. Stand firm in it.

f.g: Probably the Silas who traveled with Paul.

chapters.n: The church in “Babylon” sends greetings, as does Mark, whom Peter calls his son. Many scholars think “Babylon” is a code name for Rome.

f.g: Likely a symbolic name for Rome.
John Mark, traditionally Peter’s spiritual son and author of the Gospel of Mark.

chapters.n: Greet each other with a kiss of love—a common greeting of that culture. Peace to all who are in Christ.
